summary: Confirmed the empirical defect: run_quality_gate() in literature-convert.sh (lines 705-733) has exactly 4 checks (column-interleaving, sentence-boundary-glue, one-sided page-coverage floor, ligature/dehyphenation), none of which inspect raw content for control characters/NUL bytes/non-printable garbage. Recommended adding a printable-character-ratio check and a zero-tolerance NUL/control-char check (both operate on the content string alone, no PDF needed) as the primary fix, plus widening the existing internal page-coverage metric to a two-sided band as defense-in-depth (with a documented caveat about its likely lower sensitivity for this exact failure mode, since its numerator and denominator both derive from the same PyMuPDF extraction). literature-ingest.sh needs no logic changes - it already routes exit 3 correctly. literature-fidelity-audit.sh is a related but out-of-scope separate post-hoc batch tool with its own one-sided word_ratio floor (RATIO_THRESHOLD=0.75) against pdftotext.

artifacts.summary: Research report: gate structure, root-cause analysis of why word_ratio-vs-pdftotext is a different metric than the internal page-coverage check, and prioritized recommendations (printable-ratio check, NUL/control-char zero-tolerance check, two-sided coverage band, shared-module testability pattern).

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/literature-convert.sh, the ingest-time run_quality_gate() Python heredoc (~line 705) and the separate post-hoc literature-fidelity-audit.sh word-ratio auditor (RATIO_THRESHOLD=0.75, pdftotext-based) are two independent tools with different ground truths: the gate's internal page-coverage metric compares content against doc.get_text() from the SAME PyMuPDF-opened document, so a font-encoding corruption that corrupts extraction can corrupt both numerator and denominator similarly, masking the defect in that specific ratio even though an independent extractor (pdftotext) would show a sharp divergence. When diagnosing PDF-extraction corruption, prefer content-only checks (printable-ratio, control-char/NUL presence) over ratio-against-self-extracted-source checks, since the latter can be blind to corruption that affects both sides of the ratio equally.

literature-convert.sh uses a reusable pattern for making Python-heredoc-embedded logic unit-testable: extract shared functions into a standalone importable module (see literature_combining_overlay.py) that both the live heredoc (via sys.path.insert + import) and a --self-test CLI branch import identically, so string-only fixture tests never need a real PDF. This is the recommended approach for any new content-only quality-gate check (e.g. printable-ratio, control-char checks) since they need only a plain string, not a fitz.Document.
